name: A Simplicial Maximal Cube Exposes a Corner
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty cube family. If a maximal cube $C$ is a simplicial vertex of the maximal-cube intersection graph, then $C$ contains a vertex belonging to no other maximal cube, hence a corner. Consequently a cornerless cube family has a maximal-cube intersection graph with no simplicial vertex; that graph is nonchordal and contains an induced cycle of length at least four.
proof: The neighbours of a simplicial cube $C$ meet pairwise, and subcubes of a hypercube have the Helly property, so they share a vertex $z$ of $C$. The antipode of $z$ in $C$ lies in none of their proper traces on $C$, and a nonneighbour is disjoint from $C$. Thus this antipode belongs only to $C$. Every finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex, giving the final assertions.
